questions.prompt: What does a page object encapsulate?
options: A page's locators and the actions a user can perform on it
questions.explanation: A page object hides how to find and interact with elements behind methods named after user intent, such as loginAs().

questions.prompt: With the Page Object Model, tests should call `driver.findElement` directly whenever they need an element.
questions.explanation: Tests should talk to page objects; direct driver calls in tests scatter locators and defeat the pattern.

questions.prompt: A login action takes the user to the dashboard. What should `loginAs(user, password)` typically return?
questions.explanation: Returning the next page object models navigation and enables fluent chains such as new LoginPage(driver).loginAs(u, p).openOrders().
loginAs fills the fields, clicks submit and returns a new DashboardPage; heading() reads from the fake driver, which returns 'Dashboard'.

questions.prompt: This page object causes StaleElementReferenceException after the page refreshes. Why?
options: It finds the element once in the constructor and keeps the WebElement; after a refresh that reference is stale. Store the By locator and find the element when the method runs
The click needs a wait of 10 seconds
questions.explanation: Holding WebElements captures DOM nodes that may be replaced. Storing locators and resolving them lazily always gets the current element.

questions.prompt: Which belong in a page object? Select all that apply.
options: Methods for user actions such as search(term)
Methods that read state such as getCartCount()
Assertions about the expected business result of a test
questions.explanation: Actions and state queries belong in the page; deciding what is correct belongs in the test. Keeping assertions out lets negative and positive tests reuse the same methods.

questions.prompt: A header with search and cart icons appears on every page. How should you model it?
options: Copy its locators into every page object
As a reusable component object (e.g. Header) that pages contain
As a static utility class with global locators
questions.explanation: Component objects model repeated UI sections once and are composed into pages. Copying duplicates maintenance; static globals break with parallel drivers.

questions.prompt: Your page objects have grown to 1,500 lines each, with methods like clickButton3(). Tests are unreadable. What refactoring helps most?
options: Merge all pages into one class
Split pages into components, name methods after user intent (applyCoupon, not clickButton3), and move multi-page flows into higher-level workflow helpers
Delete the page objects and use raw driver calls
questions.explanation: Components and intent-revealing methods reduce size and make tests read like user journeys; flows spanning pages belong in a separate layer.

questions.prompt: A page has a 'Save' button that sometimes leads to the Details page and sometimes shows a validation error on the same page. How should `save()` be designed?
options: Return Object and cast in the test

Provide two intent methods, e.g. saveExpectingSuccess() returning DetailsPage and saveExpectingError() returning the same page (or expose validation state), so each test states which outcome it expects
Throw an exception from save() when errors appear
questions.explanation: The test knows which outcome it is driving, so separate methods keep both typed and readable. Always returning DetailsPage lies about the error case; Object returns lose type safety.

coding.title: Write a page object against a fake driver
coding.prompt:
A fake driver records actions: it has `fill(selector, value)`, `click(selector)` and `text(selector)`.

Write a class `LoginPage` with a constructor taking the driver, and:

- `loginAs(user, pass)`: fills `#username` and `#password`, clicks `button[type=submit]`, and returns `this`
- `errorText()`: returns the driver's text for `.error`

Tests must never see selectors, only these methods.
coding.explanation: All selectors live in one place inside the page object, so a UI change means one edit. Methods are named after intent, and returning `this` lets a negative test chain loginAs(...).errorText() without any assertion inside the page.
hints: Keep the selectors in a field on the class.
loginAs calls fill twice, then click, then returns this.

tests.name: performs actions in order
tests.code: const log = []; const d = { fill: (s, v) => log.push(['fill', s, v]), click: s => log.push(['click', s]), text: () => '' }; new LoginPage(d).loginAs('ana', 'pw'); assertEqual(log, [['fill','#username','ana'],['fill','#password','pw'],['click','button[type=submit]']])

tests.name: chains to error text
tests.code: const d = { fill(){}, click(){}, text: s => s === '.error' ? 'Wrong password' : '?' }; assertEqual(new LoginPage(d).loginAs('ana','x').errorText(), 'Wrong password')

coding.title: Page transitions and components
coding.prompt:
Build three classes using a fake driver with `click(selector)`, `fill(selector, value)` and `text(selector)`:

- `Header` (component): `cartCount()` returns `Number(driver.text('#cart-count'))`.
- `SearchPage`: has a `header` property (a Header); `search(term)` fills `#q`, clicks `#search-btn` and returns a new `ResultsPage`.
- `ResultsPage`: has a `header` too; `open(index)` clicks `.result:nth-of-type(<index+1>) a` and returns `this`; `titles()` returns `driver.text('.result h3').split('|')`.

The fake driver returns titles joined with `|`.
coding.explanation: Each page composes the Header component rather than duplicating its locators, and search() returns the next page object, so the test reads as a journey: new SearchPage(d).search('mug').titles(). Converting the count to a Number keeps assertions numeric.
hints: Header just wraps one locator and converts text to a Number.
Both pages create `this.header = new Header(driver)` in their constructor.
search() must return `new ResultsPage(this.driver)`; nth-of-type is 1-based, so use index + 1.

tests.name: search returns results page
tests.code: const log=[]; const d={ fill:(s,v)=>log.push(s+'='+v), click:s=>log.push(s), text:s=> s==='.result h3' ? 'Blue Mug|Red Mug' : '3' }; const r = new SearchPage(d).search('mug'); assert(r instanceof ResultsPage, 'search should return a ResultsPage'); assertEqual(r.titles(), ['Blue Mug','Red Mug']); assertEqual(log, ['#q=mug','#search-btn'])

tests.name: header component on both pages
tests.code: const d={ fill(){}, click(){}, text:s=> s==='#cart-count' ? '3' : 'A' }; const s = new SearchPage(d); assertEqual(s.header.cartCount(), 3); assertEqual(s.search('x').header.cartCount(), 3)

tests.name: open uses 1-based nth-of-type
tests.code: const log=[]; const d={ fill(){}, click:s=>log.push(s), text:()=>'' }; const r = new ResultsPage(d); assert(r.open(0) === r, 'open should return this'); assertEqual(log, ['.result:nth-of-type(1) a'])
